correctness.rationale: Reconstructed directly from root/leaf closed signatures. Pairwise root-versus-its-own-leaf separation forces N_G(v)∩R≠∅ for all v, precisely total domination. Every unselected root forces its private leaf selected; when two selected roots both omit their leaves, equal signatures occur exactly for closed twins within G[R]. Therefore at most one omitted leaf per twin class, contributing x^(|Q|-1)(x+|Q|). Multiplication by roots and mandatory leaves yields claimed x^n product. Isolates yield zero; nonempty disconnected graphs handled componentwise. Independent Python direct signature enumeration over every labeled G of orders 1..4 reproduces polynomial without relying on source verifier. Source verifier verify_identifying_corona.py read, but not executed as a substitute for proof.

value.rationale: A complete cardinality-generating function for identifying codes of the natural one-leaf corona graph operation answers a motivated stronger enumeration question than minimal cardinality. The total-domination/closed-twin factorization gives exact coefficients and explicit interpretation of minimum-size terms, genuinely useful as an exact combinatorial invariant for arbitrary finite G.

final_claim: For every finite nonempty undirected simple base graph G, the full identifying-code enumerator for the one-leaf corona G∘K1 equals x^n sum over total dominating R of x^(|R|-c(R)) product of (x+|Q|) over induced closed-twin classes Q of G[R]; zero if no total dominating set.
